bib.title: Chain of Hindsight aligns Language Models with Feedback
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v8, 18 Oct 2023; ICLR 2024 per caller)

question: Can a language model learn from all human feedback, positive and negative, by plain fine-tuning on feedback-conditioned sequences, without RL?
hypothesis: Conditioning language models on a sequence of generations paired with feedback and training them accordingly lets them learn to identify and correct errors and negative attributes.
contributions: CoH, a framework that uses all available feedback data without RLHF, with the same training objective as pretraining
Extensive experiments against baselines including RLHF

method.summary: Model outputs ranked by humans are turned into a text sequence with templated feedback ('Bad: ... Good: ...') and the decoder-only model is fine-tuned with the ordinary next-token loss, loss masked on feedback tokens. At inference the prompt carries positive feedback ('Good').
method.task: learning from human preference feedback (summarization, dialogue)

datasets.name: Anthropic HH (helpful and harmless)
datasets.preprocessing: for evaluation, pseudo dialogues: each model response in a previous dialogue is replaced by model output

datasets.name: TL;DR (filtered)
datasets.source: Voelske 2017, filtered by Stiennon 2020 (about 3 million posts originally)

other.note: named as a base model; sizes used and where it is used are not stated; Fig 5 varies model size

training.objective: causal LM cross-entropy on CoH sequences, loss only on non-feedback tokens, averaged over timesteps of the last model output; plus lambda-weighted pretraining log-likelihood regulariser
training.regularisation: random masking of 0% to 5% of past tokens; pretraining likelihood term on the Pile, lambda 1.5
training.hardware: inferred: TPUs (acknowledges Google TPU Research Cloud)

other.feedback_datasets_mix: three datasets combined, sampled proportionally to size
other.feedback_templates: random template per sample from Table 6 (about 30 variants)
other.same_regularisation_for_baselines: applied to CoH and all baselines

inference.samples: not stated; few-shot Table 7 averaged over 5 random seeds
inference.prompting: positive feedback token ('Good' / simple positive tokens) appended to prompt

limits: Authors: CoH sequences get long, raising training compute.
Authors: relies on costly hired human labelers; automated metrics judged less reliable.
Feedback is templated from ratings, not open-ended human language; inference uses only a positive token.
Core numbers (ROUGE, HH accuracy, scaling, Koala comparison) appear only in figures, no tables or variance; no significance tests or seeds for human eval.
Learning rate, steps/epochs, sequence length, decoding settings, hardware and compute are not stated; OPT use unclear.
Dialogue eval uses pseudo dialogues built from existing human conversations, not live chat.
Offline preference data only; online preference learning is future work.
Baselines are 6B-scale GPT-J with PPO RLHF, now dated against DPO-style methods.
